placement.position_note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 7.0 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. The whole footprint — not its centre — is tested against the platted street corridors, against its own lot lines and against every other footprint in the dataset, so no invented building of this parcel stands in the roadway; clearing the roadway is not the same as standing on a recovered lot.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: SEATED BY THE PLACEMENT POLICY'S PLATTED DEAL (data/reconstruction/1835_platted_seats.json, dealt by T-1613 and carried onto this roof by T-2136; liberties L270 and L276). NO SOURCE PLACES THIS HOUSEHOLD HERE, OR ANYWHERE. Its own record gives a name and no address — no street, no lot and not even a division — so both halves of its band were dealt rather than read, and the lot under this roof is the policy's tradesman_dwellings clause answered on the committed plat: blk_west_randolph_des_plaines#03, fronting des_plaines, a standing roof of family D4 the clause admits. THE SOURCES BELOW CARRY THE NAME AND NOTHING ELSE. The roof's own existence, position and footprint remain conjectural and are unchanged by the seating — it is still a count-unit of the 665-roof programme, adopted rather than raised, so nothing was drawn off the reconstruction order book. The household's id is carried in resident_assignment rather than in this prose, because tools/generate_dooryard_pickets.py admits a lot for a garden on an id appearing HERE and a keeper a policy deal seats is not a measurement of anybody's garden.

residents.why: boarding in the division's least crowded dwelling
residents.basis: HOUSED HERE BY THE DEAL, NOT RECORDED HERE (L354). The sources stop short of 1 July 1835 for this household and nothing puts it anywhere else; the town's rule (T-1386) counts it present, and no source says where it slept. The roof is the invention and the people are not.

persons.name: David Ingersall
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'David Ingersall' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 12, reprinted over 2 consecutive issues — dated 1834-07-09 to 1834-07-16. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

residents.why: boarding in the town's least crowded dwelling
residents.basis: HOUSED HERE BY THE DEAL, NOT RECORDED HERE (L354). This household was present in the town on 1 July 1835 and no source says where it slept; the roof is the invention and the people are not. Their card carries their evidence and is not touched by the seat.

persons.name: Baptiste De Roche
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1376, stage `underdocumented`). Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `DE ROCHE, BAPTISTE`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_020#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal. The flag retains that reason for care; the owner lifted its release block on 2026-10-16 (T-2672).

residents.research_note: WRITTEN BY tools/reconstruct_underdocumented.py (T-1376), the `native_and_metis` half of the `underdocumented` stage of the 1835 resident reconstruction programme, under the owner's ruling of 2026-09-17 recorded in AGENTS.md. This file is NOT research and is not a mint output: data/residents/households/ is re-derived by the mint writers and data/residents/index.json is derived from that directory, so a card written here lives beside the re-admissions and is overlaid onto the scene by tools/compile_scene.py. REVIEW REQUIRED AND TOUCHES REMOVAL, both true, for the subject this record is about: a Native man at Chicago in 1832, three years before the removal of the Potawatomi from this place, inside the project's first target year. Review context remains recorded; the flag does not block release under the 2026-10-16 ruling (T-2672). docs/RESEARCH/native_and_metis_1835.md lists every source read and what is still owed. docs/LIBERTIES.md carries the invention.

citations.citation: Chicago · July 1835: Building Inventory and Architectural Reconstruction Specification. Prepared for Kevin Haas, August 2026.
what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

citations.citation: The first Chicago Catholic church register — Father John Mary Irenaeus St. Cyr's marriage register and his death and burial page — as printed and annotated in the *Illinois Catholic Historical Review*, vol. 4 (July 1921 - April 1922), and republished in two pages by the Genealogy Trails Transcription Team. 128 dated marriages of 1834-1839, each naming groom, bride, witnesses and officiating priest, and 11 deaths and burials of June 1834 to March 1837.

transcribes.work: The first Chicago Catholic church record, kept by Father J. M. I. St. Cyr from 1833 and continued by Fathers Bernard Schaeffer and Timothy O'Meara to 1839
transcribes.note: THE ORIGINAL, and nobody in this project has seen it. What is read here is a 1921-22 article that prints the marriage entries and the death entries and comments on them. The article itself says the death record 'is contained on a single page' of the book.

transcribes.work: Illinois Catholic Historical Review, vol. 4 (July 1921 - April 1922)
transcribes.note: The layer actually read, at one further remove: the Genealogy Trails team transcribed these two pages out of the Review and this project read the transcription. Every record citing this source is graded transcription_mediated, twice over.

what_it_supplies: 128 marriages at Chicago (125 of them) between 1834 and 1839, each dated, and each naming its witnesses BY NAME — 513 named readings of people standing at a named place on a named day
six marriages IN THE SCENE YEAR, which with their witnesses put twenty named people in Chicago on five days of 1835
eleven deaths and burials, four of them in 1835, including the death of Thomas Owen, agent of the Indians, at Chicago on 15 October 1835
the register's own arithmetic — 22 St. Cyr marriages, 18 Schaeffer, 87 O'Meara, 1 Plunkett — which verifies any reading of it without the book
the dates bounding each priest's time at Chicago, which is what makes an unsigned entry attributable
the Irish, French and German Catholic population of the town, which is the part the poll books and letter lists reach least well
what_it_does_not_supply: any address, lot, dwelling or workplace — the register places nobody anywhere in the town
any age, except for three infants and one nine-year-old on the death page
the baptisms. The article tallies 282 of them by these same priests and prints none; that register is T-0503's object and is not in this source
residence. A marriage at Chicago on a day of 1835 is presence on that day, and presence is not residence
reliable spelling. The article says so itself: a French and German priest writing Irish and English names, and an Irish priest writing French and German ones
